**B01AF02** is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for apixaban, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) [^src1]. In the context of the Danish healthcare system, this drug code is centrally tracked by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to monitor the quality of care for patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1]. Specifically, B01AF02 is utilized as a key identifier in clinical quality indicators that measure both [[antikoagulationsbehandling|antikoagulationsbehandling]] (anticoagulation treatment) and the monitoring of kidney function in these patient populations [^src1].

As a pharmacological entity, B01AF02 belongs to the broader category of direct oral anticoagulants [^src3]. Within the national quality registries, [[antikoagulationsbehandling|antikoagulationsbehandling]] is defined to include vitamin K antagonists ([[b01aa|B01AA]]) as well as specific DOACs: dabigatran ([[b01ae07|B01AE07]]), rivaroxaban ([[b01af01|B01AF01]]), apixaban (B01AF02), and edoxaban ([[b01af03|B01AF03]]) [^src1]. The precise tracking of this code allows for standardized data collection, enabling healthcare authorities to calculate metrics such as waiting times for anticoagulation therapy and ensure adherence to evidence-based clinical standards across Danish regions [^src2].
